body.statement: Does there exist an algorithm which, for every fixed rational confidence instance \((n,\eta,\widehat p)\), returns an output list \(O\) and certificate family \(\kappa\) satisfying \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}(n,\eta,\widehat p;O,\kappa)\), terminates with delay polynomial in the input bit length and \(d\) between successive output source-forest classes, and thereby preserves the coverage conclusion of \(\text{thm:outer-fiber-confidence}\)?
body.justification: The population geometry suggests an exact output-sensitive alternative to generic semialgebraic elimination, but existence of an algorithm satisfying the certified handle specification with polynomial delay is genuinely open.
body.gap: Existing causal-model inversion papers do not exploit a source-forest quotient, and the PB-SCM papers provide point algorithms rather than certified outward enumeration.
body.consumer: A positive answer would make honest full-fiber confidence reporting computationally usable beyond very small event systems.

obligation.what_is_open: Constructing, for every rational instance \((n,\eta,\widehat p)\), an algorithm that outputs \((O,\kappa)\) satisfying \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}(n,\eta,\widehat p;O,\kappa)\), with delay polynomial in the input bit length and \(d\) and with polynomially checkable inclusion or exclusion certificates for every labeled graph.
obligation.obstruction: The source-forest theorem is pointwise in a realizable coefficient vector, whereas \(C_n\) ranges over vectors whose skeleton and head signatures can change. Exact membership of one graph is an existential nonlinear feasibility problem with strict parameter inequalities and with \(\epsilon_n=\sqrt{\log(2|I_4|/\eta)/(2n)}\). The frozen core supplies neither a polynomial-time feasibility oracle nor a complexity lower bound, so neither existence of the certified handle algorithm nor a polynomial-delay conclusion can be derived.
obligation.attempted: Reduce membership graph by graph using the reverse-topological decoder, interval screening, and source-forest enumeration. The decoder is decisive at a fixed realizable vector, but interval screening is not complete when coefficient signs can cross zero inside \(C_n\), and exhaustive graph enumeration has no polynomial-delay guarantee. Generic quantifier elimination, even after denominator clearing, also supplies no such delay bound or the required staged certificate family.
obligation.partial_result: For each fixed labeled DAG \(G\), membership \(G\in\mathcal D_n\) reduces to one finite existential feasibility problem over \(q\), \(\mu\), and \(\alpha\): impose \(q\in Q_n\), \(\mu_i>0\), \(0<\alpha_e<1\), and \(t_4(P_{G,\mu,\alpha})=T(q)\). The root-cluster recursion makes the left side polynomial in \((\mu,\alpha)\), and multiplication by the positive powers of \(q_0\) appearing in \(T\) clears every rational denominator. Thus an exact feasibility oracle followed by finite enumeration of labeled DAGs returns the exact output set \(O=\mathcal D_n\), preserving the coverage theorem. This reduction supplies neither polynomial delay nor the interval, decoding, source-forest, and branch-and-bound certificate family required by \(\mathsf A_{\mathrm{out}}\).
